newsitem.title: USA: Calif. general fund revs $600 mln above forecast.
newsitem.headline: Calif. general fund revs $600 mln above forecast.

text.p: California general fund revenues for November were $14 million above the 1996 budget projection, bringing year-to-date cash receipts to $598 million above the forecast, a state department said Tuesday.

Personal income tax receipts were $74 million above the month's forecast, while withholding was $105 million above the forecast and miscellaneous receipts were $31 million below forecast, the California Department of Finance said in its monthly state revenue report.
Sales and use tax revenues were $66 million below the month's estimate, the department said. Bank and corporation tax revenues were $55 million below the month's estimate.

Trial court revenues were up $136 million through the first four months of the fiscal year. That gain, however, is attributable to a difference in accounting and does not represent additional revenues, the department said.
The remaining revenues were $34 million above the month's forecast. This gain was driven by higher estate tax payments as well as other revenues, the Department of Finance said.
When adjusted for trial court revenues, year-to-date general fund revenues are $462 million above the forecast, the department said.
The department said an assessment of the fiscal year implications of the higher receipts was being prepared and would be released in the governor's 1997-1998 budget in early January.
